reasoning.text: The board reads instantly as an FPGA NTT accelerator: eight blue interleaved BRAM banks down the left edge, the copper multiplier column, the symmetric add/sub blocks and the natural-order FIFO capsules are all legible, and the open rail-and-brace frame keeps the datapath exposed in the ISO X-ray. The one real legibility defect the render exposes is the exploded heatsink: at y=2.75 with a 3x4 baseplate and 0.85 m fins it sits as a solid finned mass directly over the +X register column and the Barrett reduction spine, so in the ISO the right third of the datapath is visually swallowed by it and the two exploded assemblies (radix-4 BU at y~2.3-2.7 and heatsink at y~2.75) crowd the same height band. The carried-over reproducibility gaps (sigma_s crossbar permutation, XOR-fold bank/offset map, twiddle f(stage,block) addressing, FSM transition table, 9-cycle pipeline latency, negacyclic psi=1945, and the 33%/20% op-count reconciliation against the naive radix-4 baseline) are now all written into the part and metadata specs, so the scene is reproducible from itself; the remaining work is visual deconfliction, not missing facts.
gaps: Visually confirm in the next render that raising the heatsink to y=3.6/4.13 actually clears the Barrett reduction spine and the +X pipeline-register column in the ISO view; if the fins still overhang the register column, shift the heatsink stack +X toward the package edge or trim baseplate depth 4 -> 3.4.

Geometric polish (worth <2 pts): the per-lane modular adder/subtractor are plain boxes; consider a bevelled 'complex' or a thin chamfer so the sum/difference operators read as machined DSP-adjacent logic rather than generic blocks.

The exploded radix-4 BU's three W-multipliers, j-rotator torus and add/sub trees are small in the ISO; if a future pass has budget, enlarge that assembly ~15% or add a faint baseplate label edge so the W1/W2/W3 -> j -> y0..y3 dataflow is unmistakable.
Once a render confirms zero datapath occlusion and the geom box-operator nit is the only sub-2-pt item left, this scene is a legitimate converge candidate.

params.ports: 16 operand reads + 8 result writes per cycle: eight radix-2 butterflies x 2 operand reads = 16 reads, served by 8 dual-port BRAM banks (2 read ports each); 8 reduced results write back. Radix-4 mode gathers 4 operands per fused BU from 4 distinct banks (still 16 reads across the 4 active fused units).
params.per_stage_permutation: at radix-2 stage s (s=0..9) a butterfly pairs operands at indices (i, i+2^s); the crossbar applies read permutation sigma_s where operand-a of lane L is fetched from bank (L - s) mod 8 and operand-b from bank (L - s + R_s) mod 8 with R_s = ((2^s)>>3)+1; the write-back applies the inverse sigma_s^{-1} so reduced results return to their home banks
params.radix4_routing: a radix-4 BU gathers 4 operands (i, i+2^s, i+2^{s+1}, i+3*2^s) which b(i) guarantees fall in 4 distinct banks; the crossbar routes them to the 4 input ports of one fused lane-pair in a single cycle

before.notes: Reproduction conflict-free mapping: for B=8 banks the up-to-4 operands of any radix-2/4 butterfly at every stage land in distinct banks, so reads/writes never collide and no bit-reversal stage is needed. Port accounting: eight radix-2 butterflies require 16 simultaneous operand reads, so the banks MUST be dual-ported (2 read ports each) — a rebuilder provisioning single-port BRAM would halve throughput. The paper's exact bank-index/offset functions (its headline Sec. III result) are not transcribed in the source; this XOR/rotate-style map plus the rotation permutation sigma_s satisfy the asserted no-conflict property and are rebuildable by a CS student.

Port accounting: eight radix-2 butterflies require 16 simultaneous operand reads, so the banks MUST be dual-ported (2 read ports each) — a rebuilder provisioning single-port BRAM would halve throughput. [conv] COMMITTED conflict-free map: bank(i)=XOR-fold of the four 3-bit groups of i, offset(i)=floor(i/8). This is a GF(2)-linear bank function, so for any power-of-two stride 2^k the two operands differ in exactly one address bit and bank(i) XOR bank(i+2^k) = fold(2^k) != 0 -> operands always in distinct banks. [calc] FIXES the verifier counterexample of the prior map b(i)=(i+(i>>3))%8: there b(i+512)=b(i) (576 mod 8 = 0) so stride-512 operands collided; with XOR-fold fold(bit9)->bank bit0 = 1 != 0. (bank,offset) is a bijection on [0,1024) (offset fixes bits 9..3, low 3 bits XOR-map to all 8 banks). [source-missing] the paper's exact sigma_s crossbar permutation table per stage is not transcribed; the XOR-fold realizes the named property (per-stage 8-way distinctness) but may differ in routing from the paper's specific construction.

[src] Barrett mu=21843, k=28. [calc] mu=floor(2^28/12289)=21843 (12289*21843=268428627<=2^28<12289*21844). Decidability fix for the 'z3 inconclusive' counterexample: BOUND the input to x<q^2<2^28 (product of two reduced coeffs), making qh and the final correction finite/decidable. Pairs with mod_red_subshift for the conditional final subtraction.

[calc] for x<q^2 and qh=(x*mu)>>28, r=x-qh*q satisfies 0<=r<3q, so at most TWO conditional subtractions of q land r in [0,q). Stating the explicit bound (2 subtractions) is what makes the Barrett z3 query conclusive instead of 'unknown'.

params.primitive_root_psi: psi = g^6 = 11^6 mod 12289 = 1945 (order 2048; psi^1024 ≡ -1 mod 12289, i.e. negacyclic)
params.j_fourth_root: j = psi^512 (order 4, j^2 ≡ -1 ≡ 12288 mod q); used as the constant rotator by the radix-4 butterflies
params.psi_inv: psi^{-1} mod q via Fermat (psi^{q-2}); INTT uses psi^{-i}/omega^{-k} twiddles together with N^-1 = 12277
params.psi_power_table_sample: entry[k] = psi^k mod 12289 with psi=1945: psi^0=1, psi^1=1945, psi^2=10302(=omega), psi^3=6320, psi^4=3400, ...; structural anchors psi^512=j (j^2≡12288≡-1), psi^1024≡12288≡-1 (negacyclic sign flip), psi^2048≡1; the omega table is the even subsequence omega^k = psi^(2k). The full 0..2047 table is generated by iterated multiply-by-1945-mod-12289 from this seed (bit-exact, no bit-reversal indexing).
params.stored: omega^k stage twiddles for k=0..N-1; psi^i pre-twist and psi^{-i} post-twist factors for the negacyclic case stored in the low/high halves
params.addressing: address = f(stage s, butterfly-block index); one fetch reused across all 8 lanes per block
params.table_contents: entry[s][block] = omega raised to the block's stage exponent (no bit-reversal indexing); negacyclic twist factors keyed by coefficient index i

transitions: IDLE -> LOAD  [host start pulse]
LOAD -> STAGE_LOOP  [coefficient vector resident in banks]
STAGE_LOOP -> TWIDDLE_FETCH  [enter next twiddle-sharing block]
TWIDDLE_FETCH -> BUTTERFLY  [w latched onto broadcast rail]
BUTTERFLY -> REDUCE  [lane products valid]
REDUCE -> WRITEBACK  [r in [0,q) from Barrett stage]
WRITEBACK -> TWIDDLE_FETCH  [blocks remain in stage s]
WRITEBACK -> STAGE_LOOP  [stage done, s++ while s<S]
STAGE_LOOP -> INTT_STAGE_LOOP  [forward stages done AND INTT requested]
STAGE_LOOP -> DRAIN  [forward-only transform done]
INTT_STAGE_LOOP -> SCALE_N_INV  [inverse stages done]
SCALE_N_INV -> DRAIN  [coefficients scaled by N^-1]
DRAIN -> IDLE  [output FIFO emptied to host]

loop_bounds.stages_radix4: S4 = log4(N) = 5 passes, each fusing two radix-2 stages
loop_bounds.blocks_per_stage: N / 2^(s+1) groups at stage s, each sharing one twiddle factor

ops: for s in stages: for block in groups_sharing_one_twiddle: { fetch w once; parallel for bu in 0..7: butterfly(bu) }
before.notes: The factor-constant inner block is what lets one twiddle fetch be reused across all 8 lanes. The transition table and loop bounds here are reconstructed; the source asserts the 33%/20% savings only as a property and does not publish its state machine.

meta.before: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic; on the -X edge seat the host interface: a PCIe x16 gold-finger edge connector feeding a host DMA/PCIe controller block, the boundary where coefficient vectors enter and transformed results leave. 2) Drive the controller into the forward-NTT input FIFO and natural-order output FIFO, then mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks along the left edge at 1.1 m pitch between them. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel radix-2 butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register; finally seat the four carbon-fiber radix-4 fusion yokes in the open gap between the multiplier and add/sub columns, each binding a lane-pair (0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7) into one fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit so the eight radix-2 lanes reconfigure into four radix-4 BUs. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member abutting it, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column (grounded by its own standoff onto the array frame), keeping the read, return and twiddle channels on three separate heights; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the elevated rail spanning the multiplier column (grounded by a standoff onto the array frame) so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one fused radix-4 butterfly unit onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (three twiddle multipliers W1/W2/W3 -> constant j-rotator -> y0..y3 add/sub tree -> four-output register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view, and clamp the ten-fin exploded aluminum heatsink onto its riser stub above the die.
